name: The service serves its own leaf certificate at an anonymous route, and the set-up dialog shows its fingerprint
aliases: server certificate fingerprint in the set-up dialog
summary: A service started with --cert/--key answers GET /v1/service/certificate without a log-in with {"certificate": "<PEM>", "sha256": "<fingerprint>"}: the certificate is the LEAF re-encoded by the kit from the loaded file's first CERTIFICATE block, and the fingerprint is that leaf's SHA-256 DER hash in the colon form openssl x509 -noout -fingerprint -sha256 prints. The route never echoes the file. A combined key-and-certificate PEM (a supported start), a TRUSTED CERTIFICATE block, an openssl x509 -text dump, bag attributes and comments cannot reach the answer, and the private key is never served. The file is read as bytes (a Latin-1 comment must not stop the service) and the read is capped (1 MiB of file, 64 kB of base64 per block); a file with no leaf leaves the service running with the route answering the ordinary 404, as plain http and the tunnel do. The set-up dialog reads the route, shows the fingerprint and offers a Save button, and says what comparing it proves and does not; the set-up prompt writes no VS Code settings and no certificate file, and puts the '# server = ADDRESS' line (and the fingerprint) into the credential file's own content, idempotently, each on its own line.
